thread.title: Quarterly Overview Apple ( AAPL ) reported FQ1 revenue of $8

author: Jeremy McKinzie
title: Quarterly Overview Apple ( AAPL ) reported FQ1 revenue of $8
text:
Quarterly Overview Apple ( AAPL ) reported FQ1 revenue of $88.3 billion, exceeding consensus estimates by $670 million. Revenue additionally exceeded my estimate of $85.3 billion, with the beat driven by strength from the iPhone lineup, notably iPhone X. EPS also exceeded consensus by $0.04 due to revenue outperformance. With noise in the quarter surrounding softness in iPhone X units, Apple still managed to beat top line consensus despite a 1% y/y drop in iPhone units due to a higher ASP of $796. The midpoint of guidance for FQ2 came in below consensus, but noting historical conservative guidance and an expected sequential accelerated sell-through in the coming quarter, there could be some upside to FQ2 numbers. While investors digest a likely reset on iPhone unit expectations for F2018, I would use a pullback as a buying opportunity, noting higher iPhone ASPs, continual Services growth and tailwinds from increased capital allocation, as compelling anchors to be a buyer at these levels. I maintain my Buy rating on Apple with a 12-month price target of $196, implying 22.1% upside.
A Strong Cycle With Higher Prices iPhone revenue was $61.5 billion, up 13.2% y/y on units sold of 77.3 million, down 1.2% y/y, higher than my revenue estimate of $59.8 billion on 89.2 million units sold. The slight decline in units y/y and soft guidance for FQ2 may lead to some downward revisions in the current iPhone cycle, which I acknowledge as my own F2018 unit estimates come down from 255 million to 220 million. Management noted on the call that the soft sell through for the iPhone X in the quarter was driven by the timing shift of a later release in November, relative to a usual September launch. This could lead to higher demand in FQ2, as the company is expecting an accelerated sequential increase in iPhone sell through in the March quarter. I estimate 51.7 million iPhones sold in FQ2, a 2% y/y increase on revenue of $38.9 billion, up 17% y/y, for an ASP of $751.
Softness in iPhone units may be indicative of a longer upgrade cycle from the existing install base, but I believe iPhone saturation could be offset by higher ASPs over time. An iPhone super cycle may not materialize, but a strong cycle with higher prices may be playing out, which will likely still augment both the top and bottom lines. A longer upgrade cycle could be somewhat furthered in 2018 by Apple lowering the cost to replace existing batteries, but I believe that also will be mitigated by higher ASPs. I forecast iPhone revenue will be $162.2 billion in F2018, for growth of 14.8% y/y.
Servicing up All Time Records The Apple Store, Apple Music, iCloud and Apple Pay had their best quarter ever in revenue. Services revenue of $8.4 billion, up 18.1% y/y, fell shy of my estimates of $8.8 billion. Management noted the number of paid subscriptions across services passed 240 million at the end of FQ1, as Services continues to grow and generate recurring revenue for Apple. Growth in merchant adoption of Apple Pay is up over 50% y/y, and with Apple having launched peer to peer payments, and the upcoming release of HomePod compatible with Apple Music, the iOS platform continues its stickiness for users. Apple remains on track to double its 2016 service revenue by 2020, and with several offerings within Services achieving record quarterly revenues, it certainly continues to be easily achievable in my opinion.
While likely not impactful in the short term, the Copyright Royalty Board ruled that songwriters will see a 50% increase over five years in payments for interactive streaming. While this may be insignificant to Apple’s bottom line, I wouldn’t rule out a gradual increase in pricing to Apple Music over time, as Apple may adjust their pricing if the costs of streaming content moves higher. I estimate Apple will generate service revenue of $8.8 billion in FQ2, up 25% y/y on continued strength across the board.
Seeing iPad Growth and Stable PC Market Share The iPad segment posted revenue of $5.8 billion, up 5.9% y/y, on units of 13.1 million, up 0.7% y/y, exceeding my estimate of $4.8 billion on 12.4 million units sold. This is the iPad’s third straight quarter of growth, bolstered by strength from the iPad and iPad Pro. Management mentioned on the call they gained share in nearly every market and called out strength in emerging markets. iPad revenue could continue to grow with expanding enterprise adoption, as Apple noted that LensCrafters will be using over 7,000 iPad Pros for their business. Mac generated revenue of $6.8 billion in revenue, down 4.8% y/y, on units of 5.1 million, down 4.9% y/y. This was lower than my estimate of $8 billion on 5.4 million units sold. IDC estimated Apple gained 0.5% in market share y/y in the PC market in CQ4 2017 and remained in fourth place. iPad revenue could be $4.1 billion in FQ2, up 7% on 8.9 million units sold, augmented by continued strength in emerging markets. I estimate Mac revenue will be $5.6 billion in FQ2, down 4% y/y, on 4.1 million units sold, down 2% y/y, affected by continual weakness in U.S. PC sales, partially offset by strength in emerging markets.

Other Products Other Products revenue was $5.4 billion, up 36.4%, driven by strength in Apple Watch, which grew over 50% growth in revenue and units y/y. Other products revenue could be $3.8 billion in FQ2, up 35% y/y.
Putting Cash to Work Thanks to new tax legislation, it has become conducive for Apple to repatriate its offshore cash. Management estimates making a $38 billion payment to the U.S. government on cumulative past foreign earnings. As Apple ended the quarter with $285.1 billion in cash and marketable securities, it would leave the company with $247 billion in cash. The company announced it would provide specific detail on capital allocation plans when it reports FQ2 results, and I continue to believe share repurchases and an increase in the dividend are the two most likely options.
However, I continue to believe a large acquisition could be possible to diversify away from reliance on the iPhone and provide Apple with multiple expansion. I previously mentioned Disney ( DIS ) would be a compelling target, and given Disney’s recent acquisition of Fox’s ( FOXA ) film assets, that further entrenches my thinking. Apple’s partnering with Steven Spielberg on one of his projects, and the Wall Street Journal estimates Apple will spend $1 billion on original content over the course of this year. An acquisition of Disney would make Apple a significant original content owner and accomplish diversification outside the iOS ecosystem. With CBS ( CBS ) original content and noteworthy TV ratings, they would also be a less costly but beneficial target, as I’ve mentioned prior, especially as they may be scaling up with a Viacom ( VIA ) re-merger. For FQ2, I estimate Apple will generate $61.3 billion in revenue, up 16% y/y and operating income of $16 billion, up 13.6% y/y.
Risks Apple remains largely tied to consumer spending. An economic slowdown would impact its top-line growth. Failure to innovate on a technological front could cause consumers to go elsewhere to a number of competitors. If the iPhone loses popularity with consumers, this would materially impact Apple’s business. Current litigation risk with Qualcomm (NASDAQ: QCOM ), while highly unlikely, could lead to a ban on iPhone imports, which would be very materially adverse to the overall business. As Apple seeks to put repatriated cash to work, it may seek to acquire companies outside of its core competency and/or overpay, creating acquisition risk.
Valuation For F2018, I estimate Apple will generate $262.5 billion in sales, up 14.5% y/y, led by the iPhone 8 and X models and operating income of $67.7 billion, up 10.4% y/y, due to higher revenue and increased average selling prices driven by the iPhone X. Apple trades at 14.8x F2018E EPS, 13.1x F2018E free cash flow, and 13.3x F2018E operating income. Assigning a blended multiple of 18x F2018 EPS, 16x F2018E free cash flow and 16x F2018E operating income, results in a price target of $196, implied upside of 22.1%.
